sounds.name: Flute Organ
sounds.ref: In the style of a soft chapel organ
sounds.blurb: A gentle organ tone with a slow, living shimmer from one oscillator drifting against the other.
sounds.how: A triangle and a quiet square an octave up are like two soft organ stops. DECAY OFF makes the notes start and stop like an organ’s. The shimmer comes from VCO 1 MOD OFF: the LFO wobbles VCO 2 alone, so it drifts very slightly against a steady VCO 1.

steps.title: Two soft stops
steps.why:
A triangle and a quiet square an octave up act like two soft organ stops. VCO stands for voltage-controlled oscillator.
- VCO 1 WAVEFORM 0, VOLUME 7.5: a triangle, the soft main stop, through its own VCA (voltage-controlled amplifier).
- VCO 2 FREQUENCY 6 (+12 st), WAVEFORM 6.7: a square an octave up, hollow and reedy.
- VCO 2 VOLUME 3.5: the upper stop, quieter. Higher is brighter and reedier.
- Listen for: a soft, hollow, organ-like tone.

steps.title: Organ on and off
steps.why:
Organs start and stop at once. The VCF (voltage-controlled filter) stays gentle, and ADS 1, the loudness envelope (attack, decay, sustain), is set up like a switch.
- VCF FREQ 6.5 (1.4 kHz), RESONANCE 0: a soft filter with no peak. KEYB CTRL at 1 (100 %) makes it follow the keys, and ADS CONTROL at 0 (off) means no filter envelope.
- ADS 1 ATTACK 2.5 (8 ms): nearly instant, just enough to avoid a click.
- ADS 1 SUSTAIN 10: full level while held.
- DECAY OFF on: sets decay and release to zero, so notes stop as soon as you let go.
- Listen for: the organ’s clean stop. Switch DECAY OFF off and set DECAY to 8 for a church-like ring after each chord.

steps.title: A shimmer on VCO 2 only
steps.why:
The LFO (low-frequency oscillator) is wired to both VCOs’ pitch. VCO 1 MOD OFF leaves VCO 1 out, so only VCO 2 moves and the two stops drift very slightly against each other.
- VCO 1 MOD OFF on: VCO 1 stays steady, so the LFO makes a shimmer instead of a vibrato.
- LFO triangle, RATE 6 (2.51 Hz): a smooth, slow waver.
- LFO VOLUME 1 (10 %): how far VCO 2 drifts. Keep it low; above 2 the organ sounds out of tune.
- Listen for: a gentle beating in held chords. Switch VCO 1 MOD OFF off and it becomes a plain vibrato.

context.mod.vco1Off: In this sound: keeps VCO 1 steady, so the LFO makes a shimmer instead of a vibrato.
context.lfo.volume: In this sound: how far VCO 2 drifts. Keep it low; above 2 the organ sounds out of tune.
context.ads1.decayOff: In this sound: the organ’s clean stop. Switch it off and set DECAY to 8 for a church-like ring after each chord.
context.vca2.level: In this sound: the upper stop. Higher is brighter and reedier.

tweaks.try: Switch off, with ADS 1 DECAY at 8
tweaks.hear: Each note rings on after release, as if in a large hall.
The upper stop a fifth higher: an old, hollow organ colour.

sounds.name: Mirrored Morph Pad
sounds.ref: The voltage processor as a splitter and inverter
sounds.blurb: A slow pad in which one oscillator brightens while the other softens, back and forth.
sounds.how: The LFO goes into the voltage processor. Its OUT carries the LFO as it is, to VCO 1 WAVEFORM; REV OUT carries it upside down, to VCO 2 WAVEFORM. So as VCO 1 turns from triangle towards pulse, VCO 2 turns the other way, and the pad keeps changing colour without ever getting much louder or brighter overall. Only a synth whose waveform can be swept by a voltage can do this.

steps.title: Two oscillators, an octave apart
steps.why:
Two VCOs (voltage-controlled oscillators) are parked in the middle of their WAVEFORM travel, so a voltage can later swing them either way.
- WAVEFORM 4.5 on both: a little before sawtooth. The Kobol’s WAVEFORM knob turns smoothly from triangle to pulse, so from here each can move towards either end.
- VCO 2 FREQUENCY 4 (−12 st): an octave down, for body.
- VCO 2 BEAT 0.4 (+4 cents): a slow beat against VCO 1.
- VOLUME 7 and 6.5: each VCO has its own VCA (voltage-controlled amplifier) in place of a mixer.
- Listen for: a warm, buzzy octave tone that does not move yet.

steps.title: The LFO into the voltage processor
steps.why:
The voltage processor adds and scales control voltages. Here it carries the LFO (low-frequency oscillator) and sets its depth, ready to send it two ways.
- Cable LFO OUT 2 → IN 2: OUT 2 is the LFO at full level, into the voltage processor’s second input.
- IN 1 GAIN 0: IN 1 carries +10 V when nothing is plugged in. At 0 it adds nothing, so the sweep stays centred.
- OUT GAIN 0.4: the depth of both sweeps at once, as it scales OUT and REV OUT together.
- LFO triangle, RATE 2.8 (0.13 Hz): a smooth cycle of about eight seconds.
- LFO VOLUME 0: no vibrato on the VCOs.
- Listen for: no change yet; nothing takes the voltage processor’s output.

steps.title: One shape up, the other down
steps.why:
OUT carries the LFO as it is; REV OUT carries it upside down. Patched to the two WAVEFORM inputs, one oscillator brightens while the other softens.
- Cable OUT → VCO 1 WAVEFORM: the voltage processor’s output. VCO 1 swings towards pulse and back towards triangle with the LFO.
- Cable REV OUT → VCO 2 WAVEFORM: VCO 2 gets the same movement reversed, so it always goes the other way.
- Listen for: a pad that keeps changing colour without getting much brighter or louder overall. Pull one cable to hear a plain one-way sweep instead.

steps.title: Soft filter, slow swell
steps.why:
The VCF (voltage-controlled filter) trims the bright end of the sweep, and ADS 1, the loudness envelope (attack, decay, sustain), makes each chord swell in and fade.
- VCF FREQ 6 (1.0 kHz), RESONANCE 1.5: takes the harsh top off the pulse end, with a slight edge.
- KEYB CTRL 1 (100 %), ADS CONTROL 0 (off): the cutoff follows the keys, with no filter envelope.
- ADS 1 ATTACK 8 (840 ms): a slow swell into each chord.
- DECAY 9 (2.0 s), SUSTAIN 10: full level while held, and a two-second fade after release, since DECAY is also the release.
- Listen for: chords that swell in, drift for as long as you hold them, then fade.

context.vp.in1: In this sound: at 0. Turn it up and the built-in +10 V pushes VCO 1 brighter and VCO 2 softer, off centre.
context.lfo.rate: In this sound: how slowly the two oscillators trade places.
context.vco1.wave: In this sound: the centre of VCO 1’s sweep.
context.vco2.wave: In this sound: the centre of VCO 2’s sweep, which runs the opposite way.
context.ads1.attack: In this sound: the slow swell into each chord.

tweaks.hear: Both sweeps go right to the ends: triangle against narrow pulse.

The two oscillators swap shapes in jumps, like two organ stops being pulled in turn.

sounds.name: Slow Bloom
sounds.ref: An envelope on one oscillator’s VCA
sounds.blurb: Each note starts as a pure, soft tone and slowly blooms into a rich, bright chord tone.
sounds.how: VCO 1 is a steady triangle. VCO 2, a sawtooth an octave up, has its VOLUME at 0 and ADS 2 OUT patched to its VOLUME input, with a slow attack. So each note starts as the plain triangle and VCO 2 fades in over two seconds or so, while the same envelope opens the filter a little. It is a crossfade from one oscillator to the other, played by an envelope.

steps.title: A pure triangle
steps.why:
VCO 1 (a voltage-controlled oscillator, the part that makes the raw tone) is the plain start of every note.
- VCO 1 WAVEFORM 0: fully left, a pure triangle.
- VCO 1 VOLUME 7: its level into the filter through its own VCA (voltage-controlled amplifier).
- Listen for: a soft, flute-like tone.

steps.title: A sawtooth waiting in VCO 2
steps.why:
VCO 2 is set up as the bloom: a brighter voice waiting at 0, to be faded in by an envelope.
- VCO 2 FREQUENCY 6 (+12 st): an octave up.
- VCO 2 WAVEFORM 5: sawtooth, bright and full. Try the pulse end for a reedier bloom.
- VCO 2 BEAT 0.3 (+3 cents): a touch sharp, for slow movement against VCO 1.
- VCO 2 VOLUME 0: silent until ADS 2 opens its VCA.
- Listen for: no change yet.

steps.title: ADS 2 fades VCO 2 in
steps.why:
ADS 2, an ADS (attack, decay, sustain) envelope, is patched to VCO 2’s VCA with a slow attack: a crossfade from one oscillator to the other, played by an envelope.
- Cable ADS 2 OUT → VCO 2 VOLUME: the envelope opens VCO 2’s VCA on top of its knob at 0.
- ATTACK 9.2 (2.3 s): VCO 2 fades in over about two seconds. At 1 the saw is there from the start.
- DECAY 9.5 (3.0 s), SUSTAIN 7: after the peak it eases back to 70 %, so most of the sawtooth stays.
- ADS CONTROL 1 (+1.4 oct): the same envelope opens the filter a little, so the bloom brightens as well as thickens.
- Listen for: hold a note for three seconds: a pure tone slowly grows into a rich, buzzy one.

steps.title: Soft filter, gentle loudness
steps.why:
The VCF (voltage-controlled filter) sits low, and ADS 1, the loudness envelope, gives a soft start and a long release.
- VCF FREQ 5.5 (715 Hz), RESONANCE 1: fairly dark, so the sawtooth comes in warm rather than harsh.
- KEYB CTRL 1 (100 %): keyboard control; the cutoff follows the notes.
- ADS 1 ATTACK 6.5 (230 ms): a soft fade-in.
- ADS 1 DECAY 9 (2.0 s), SUSTAIN 10: full level while held, then a two-second release.
- Listen for: short notes stay soft and pure; only held notes bloom.

sounds.name: Solo Cello
sounds.ref: In the style of a slow solo cello line
sounds.blurb: A warm, bowed string with a soft start and a gentle vibrato.
sounds.how: A sawtooth gives the rich, buzzing tone of a bowed string, and a triangle an octave below gives it weight. ADS 2 opens the filter a little as each note is bowed in, and ADS 1’s slow attack stops the notes from starting with a click. A small, slow LFO on both VCOs is the player’s vibrato.

steps.title: Sawtooth with a triangle below
steps.why:
A sawtooth gives the rich, buzzing tone of a bowed string, and a triangle an octave below gives it weight. VCO stands for voltage-controlled oscillator.
- VCO 1 WAVEFORM 4.6: just short of sawtooth, bright and buzzy.
- VCO 1 VOLUME 7.5: its level through its own VCA (voltage-controlled amplifier).
- VCO 2 FREQUENCY 4 (−12 st), WAVEFORM 0.5: close to a triangle, an octave down.
- VCO 2 VOLUME 5: the body under the bowed tone.
- Listen for: a buzzy tone with a round low end beneath it.

steps.title: A bowed filter
steps.why:
The VCF (voltage-controlled filter) sits fairly low, and ADS 2, the filter envelope (attack, decay, sustain), opens it a little as the bow bites.
- VCF FREQ 4.6 (384 Hz), RESONANCE 2: the warmth of the tone. Higher is closer to a viola or violin.
- KEYB CTRL 0.8 (80 %): keyboard control; the cutoff mostly follows the notes, so high notes are slightly mellower.
- ADS CONTROL 1.2 (+1.7 oct): a modest opening on each note.
- ADS 2 ATTACK 6.8 (300 ms): a slowish rise, like the bow biting.
- ADS 2 DECAY 8 (840 ms), SUSTAIN 6: settles most of the way back, so held notes keep some edge.
- Listen for: each note brightening slightly just after it starts.

steps.title: A slow bow
steps.why:
ADS 1, the loudness envelope for the output VCA, gives a slow bow into each note.
- ATTACK 6.6 (260 ms): about a quarter of a second, so notes start without a click. Longer gives a softer entry.
- DECAY 8.4 (1.2 s), SUSTAIN 9: near-full level while held, and a medium release after, as DECAY is also the release.
- Listen for: notes that ease in and hang on slightly after you let go, joining a slow line.

steps.title: Vibrato
steps.why:
The LFO (low-frequency oscillator) is wired to both VCOs’ pitch, and LFO VOLUME is the vibrato depth. A small, even vibrato is the player’s hand.
- LFO WAVEFORM triangle: a smooth waver.
- LFO RATE 6.6 (4.37 Hz): about four wavers a second.
- LFO VOLUME 1.2 (12 %): small. Above 2 it sounds more like a theremin than a cello.
- Listen for: a gentle vibrato on held notes. Set VOLUME to 0 to hear how static it is without.

sounds.name: Distant Horn
sounds.ref: In the style of a French horn in a film score
sounds.blurb: A soft, round horn that swells into each note, as if heard from across a valley.
sounds.how: Two ramps, between triangle and sawtooth, give a mellower tone than the sawtooths of a synth brass. The filter sits low and ADS 2 opens it slowly, so each note warms up after it starts. A soft attack on ADS 1 and a little vibrato make it breathe.

steps.title: Two mellow ramps
steps.why:
Two ramps, between triangle and sawtooth, give a mellower tone than the sawtooths of a synth brass. VCO stands for voltage-controlled oscillator.
- WAVEFORM 3.4 on both: past triangle, well short of sawtooth. Towards 5 it turns into a brassier trumpet.
- VOLUME 7 and 6: each VCO has its own VCA (voltage-controlled amplifier) in place of a mixer.
- VCO 2 BEAT 0.6 (+6 cents): slightly off, as two players are never quite together.
- Listen for: a soft, rounded buzz with slow beating.

steps.title: A dark, slowly opening filter
steps.why:
The VCF (voltage-controlled filter) sits low and ADS 2, the filter envelope (attack, decay, sustain), opens it slowly, so each note warms up after it starts.
- VCF FREQ 3.8 (221 Hz), RESONANCE 1: dark, which gives the sense of distance. Lower sounds further away.
- KEYB CTRL 1 (100 %): keyboard control; the cutoff follows the notes.
- ADS CONTROL 1.8 (+2.5 oct): how much each note brightens.
- ADS 2 ATTACK 6.8 (300 ms): the slow warm-up.
- ADS 2 DECAY 8 (840 ms), SUSTAIN 5: settles half way back, so held notes stay partly open.
- Listen for: a muffled start that swells brighter over about a third of a second.

steps.title: A soft breath in
steps.why:
ADS 1, the loudness envelope, gives a soft breath into each note, and the LFO (low-frequency oscillator) adds a slight vibrato.
- ADS 1 ATTACK 6.4 (220 ms): about a fifth of a second of fade-in.
- ADS 1 DECAY 8 (840 ms), SUSTAIN 10: full level while held and a soft release, as DECAY is also the release.
- LFO triangle, RATE 6.3 (3.31 Hz): a slow, smooth waver.
- LFO VOLUME 0.8 (8 %): just enough vibrato to sound played. The LFO is wired to both VCOs’ pitch.
- Listen for: notes that swell in and sound distant and alive.

sounds.name: Lonely Voice
sounds.ref: A wordless singing voice from one resonant filter
sounds.blurb: A breathy, vowel-like voice singing a slow melody.
sounds.how: A voice’s vowel comes from resonances that stay put while the pitch changes. Here the filter has plenty of resonance and follows the keys only a little, so its peak stays in roughly the same place: a fixed vowel. The breath is the noise generator, which has no level knob of its own, so it goes through the voltage processor and OUT GAIN sets how much reaches the filter. A slow attack and a small vibrato make it sing.

steps.title: A sawtooth
steps.why:
A sawtooth has every harmonic, which gives the resonant filter plenty to pick a vowel from. VCO stands for voltage-controlled oscillator.
- VCO 1 WAVEFORM 4.8: almost a sawtooth.
- VCO 1 VOLUME 7: its level through its own VCA (voltage-controlled amplifier).
- VCO 2 VOLUME 0: off.
- Listen for: a plain, buzzy tone.

steps.title: A fixed, resonant vowel
steps.why:
A voice’s vowel comes from resonances that stay put while the pitch changes. Here the VCF (voltage-controlled filter) has plenty of resonance and follows the keys only a little: a fixed vowel.
- VCF FREQ 5.3 (622 Hz): the vowel. Lower sounds like “oo”, higher like “ah” and then “ee”.
- RESONANCE 6.5: a strong peak that makes the tone vocal. Too high and it starts to whistle.
- KEYB CTRL 0.3 (30 %): keyboard control, low, so the peak barely moves from note to note.
- ADS CONTROL 0 (off): no filter envelope, so the vowel is steady.
- Listen for: a nasal, vowel-like tone. Sweep VCF FREQ slowly to hear the vowel change.

steps.title: Breath through the voltage processor
steps.why:
The noise generator has no level knob and is not wired in, so it goes through the voltage processor, a utility that adds and scales voltages. OUT GAIN then acts as a volume knob for the breath.
- NOISE OUT → IN 2, OUT → VCF AUDIO IN: two cables; the noise passes through the voltage processor into the filter, alongside VCO 1.
- Noise colour white: bright, then filtered down by the vowel.
- IN 1 GAIN 0: stops IN 1’s built-in +10 V adding a steady voltage, which would only give a thump at each note.
- OUT GAIN 0.15: low, so the noise is a breath under the tone rather than a hiss over it.
- Listen for: a breathy edge on the voice. Raise OUT GAIN to hear it turn into a whisper.

steps.title: Breathe and sing
steps.why:
ADS 1, the loudness envelope (attack, decay, sustain), gives a slow breath in, and the LFO (low-frequency oscillator) is the singer’s vibrato.
- ADS 1 ATTACK 7 (360 ms): a slow start, like a singer easing in.
- ADS 1 DECAY 8.5 (1.3 s), SUSTAIN 10: full level while held, then a long release.
- LFO triangle, RATE 6.7 (4.79 Hz): a natural vibrato speed.
- LFO VOLUME 1.4 (14 %): the vibrato depth on the VCO’s pitch.
- Listen for: a slow melody that sounds sung. Leave gaps between phrases, as a singer would breathe.

sounds.name: Bright Racing Arpeggio
sounds.ref: In the style of Daft Punk — "Aerodynamic"
sounds.blurb: A fast, bright arpeggio that tumbles down each chord, with a sharp, glassy edge on the front of every note.
sounds.how: VCO 1 is between ramp and sawtooth, with VCO 2 an octave up as a quieter square for sparkle. The filter is left fairly open and follows the keys, so high notes stay as bright as low ones. The Kobol’s own trick does the rest: ADS 2 OUT is patched into VCO 1 WAVEFORM, so each note starts as a thin, bright pulse and morphs back towards the sawtooth as the envelope falls. That gives every note a crisp pick without a sharper filter.

steps.title: A sawtooth and a square an octave up
steps.why:
VCO 1 is the main tone and VCO 2 a quieter square an octave up for sparkle. VCO stands for voltage-controlled oscillator.
- VCO 1 WAVEFORM 4: on the ramp, just before the sawtooth. Nearer 0 the notes will settle softer.
- VCO 2 WAVEFORM 6.7: a square, hollow and bright.
- VCO 2 FREQUENCY 6 (+12 st): an octave up.
- VOLUME 7.5 and 4.5: each VCO has its own VCA (voltage-controlled amplifier). Too much VCO 2 and it takes over the pitch.
- Listen for: a bright, buzzy tone with a sparkle on top.

steps.title: A bright, tracking filter
steps.why:
The VCF (voltage-controlled filter) is left fairly open and follows the keys, so high notes stay as bright as low ones.
- VCF FREQ 6.8 (1.8 kHz), RESONANCE 2: fairly open, with a slight edge.
- KEYB CTRL 1 (100 %): keyboard control; the brightness stays even across the arpeggio.
- ADS CONTROL 1.5 (+2.1 oct): ADS 2, the filter envelope, adds a flick on each note.
- Listen for: a small flick at the start of each note, from ADS 2’s starting shape.

steps.title: A quick envelope
steps.why:
ADS 2 is an ADS (attack, decay, sustain) envelope. Made short, it is the shape of the pick on each note, and in the next step it drives the waveform as well as the filter.
- ATTACK 1 (2 ms): immediate.
- DECAY 4.5 (43 ms): very short; how long the bright pick lasts.
- SUSTAIN 0: gone completely while the key is held.
- Listen for: a tight, bright click on each note in place of the softer flick.

steps.title: Patch the envelope to the waveform
steps.why:
The Kobol’s own trick: ADS 2 is patched to VCO 1’s WAVEFORM input, so each note starts further along the knob’s path, at the thin pulse end, and slides back to where the knob is set.
- Cable ADS 2 OUT → VCO 1 WAVEFORM: the envelope pushes the shape towards pulse on each note; the knob at 4 is where it settles.
- Listen for: a crisp, glassy edge on the front of every note, a pick without a sharper filter. Pull the cable out and back in to compare.

steps.title: Short, even notes
steps.why:
ADS 1, the loudness envelope for the output VCA, keeps fast notes separate.
- ATTACK 1 (2 ms): instant.
- DECAY 4.8 (55 ms), SUSTAIN 6: a quick dip to a held level of 60 %, which adds punch. DECAY is also the release, so notes stop about 50 ms after you let go.
- Listen for: a tight, even arpeggio at speed. Raise DECAY and the notes start to run together.

sounds.name: Slowly Opening Pulse
sounds.ref: In the style of Kraftwerk — "Metropolis"
sounds.blurb: A dark, steady pulse of short bass notes whose filter opens and closes very slowly over many bars.
sounds.how: Two oscillators, a sawtooth and a square an octave below, go through the 24 dB filter set low with some resonance. Short envelopes with no sustain turn each note into a firm pulse. The slow opening comes from the LFO, but not straight in: LFO OUT 2 goes through the voltage processor, whose OUT GAIN sets how far it moves the filter, and from there into VCF FREQUENCY. LFO VOLUME stays at 0, so the notes do not wobble in pitch.

steps.title: A sawtooth over a square
steps.why:
A sawtooth over a square an octave below gives a dark, solid pulse. VCO stands for voltage-controlled oscillator.
- VCO 1 WAVEFORM 5: sawtooth, bright and buzzy.
- VCO 2 WAVEFORM 6.7, FREQUENCY 4 (−12 st): a square an octave below, for weight.
- VCO 2 BEAT 0.4 (+4 cents): a very slight beat against VCO 1.
- VOLUME 7 and 6: each VCO has its own VCA (voltage-controlled amplifier) in place of a mixer.
- Listen for: a thick, hollow, buzzy low tone.

steps.title: A dark, resonant filter
steps.why:
The VCF (voltage-controlled filter) goes low with resonance, and a little envelope gives each note a push.
- VCF FREQ 5.2 (581 Hz): the middle of the slow sweep to come.
- RESONANCE 5: a ringing edge that will grow as the filter opens.
- KEYB CTRL 0.5 (50 %): keyboard control at half, so higher notes open a little.
- ADS CONTROL 1.5 (+2.1 oct): ADS 2, the filter envelope, gives each note a soft push.
- Listen for: a darker, resonant tone.

steps.title: Short pulses
steps.why:
Both ADS (attack, decay, sustain) envelopes get no attack, a short decay and no sustain, so each note is a pulse of the same length.
- ADS 2 ATTACK 1, DECAY 4.6, SUSTAIN 0: a 2 ms rise and a 46 ms fall. A quick filter push at the front of every note.
- ADS 1 ATTACK 1, DECAY 6, SUSTAIN 0: a 2 ms rise and a 150 ms fall. ADS 1 is the loudness. Each note lasts about 150 ms, however long the key is held.
- Listen for: firm, even pulses. Change ADS 1 DECAY to make them shorter or longer.

steps.title: A very slow LFO, kept off the pitch
steps.why:
The LFO (low-frequency oscillator) is set very slow, ready to open the filter over many bars, and kept off the pitch.
- LFO WAVEFORM triangle: a smooth rise and fall.
- LFO RATE 2.2 (0.08 Hz): about twelve seconds per cycle. Lower is slower.
- LFO VOLUME 0: the LFO reaches both VCOs’ pitch through this knob; at 0 the notes do not wobble. LFO OUT 2 still carries it at full level.
- Listen for: no change yet; the LFO is not patched anywhere.

steps.title: Through the voltage processor to the filter
steps.why:
The voltage processor, a utility that adds and scales voltages, sits between the LFO and the filter, so its OUT GAIN sets how far the LFO moves the cutoff.
- LFO OUT 2 → IN 2, OUT → VCF FREQUENCY: two cables; the full-level LFO goes through the voltage processor to the cutoff.
- IN 1 GAIN 0: removes the fixed +10 V that IN 1 carries when unpatched, so only the LFO reaches the filter.
- OUT GAIN 0.25: the depth of the sweep. At 0 the pulse stays dark.
- Listen for: over several bars the pulse brightens and its resonant edge grows, then it sinks back.

sounds.name: Rubber Scoop Bass
sounds.ref: In the style of Parliament — "Rumpofsteelskin" (Motor Booty Affair)
sounds.blurb: A bouncy, squelching funk bass where every note scoops up into pitch from just below.
sounds.how: A sawtooth over a square an octave down goes through a resonant filter that ADS 2 flicks open on every note. The same envelope, turned upside down by the voltage processor, is patched into VCO MOD IN, so each note starts a few semitones flat and springs up to pitch as the envelope falls. The scoop and the squelch move together, which gives the rubbery bounce of a funk synth bass. The Kobol has no glide, so this is how it slides.

steps.title: A sawtooth over a square
steps.why:
A sawtooth over a square an octave down gives the bass bite and weight. VCO stands for voltage-controlled oscillator.
- VCO 1 WAVEFORM 5: sawtooth at the note played, the bright top.
- VCO 2 WAVEFORM 6.7, FREQUENCY 4 (−12 st): a square an octave below, for the bottom end.
- VOLUME 8 and 6: each VCO has its own VCA (voltage-controlled amplifier) in place of a mixer.
- Listen for: a thick, buzzy bass tone.

steps.title: A resonant, closed filter
steps.why:
The VCF (voltage-controlled filter) is closed with a strong resonant peak for the envelope to push around.
- VCF FREQ 3.4 (168 Hz): dark between notes.
- RESONANCE 6: a wet, vocal peak. Above 8 it starts to whistle.
- KEYB CTRL 0.7 (70 %): keyboard control; higher notes open somewhat, but not fully.
- Listen for: a muffled bass with a hollow ring.

steps.title: A quick squelch from ADS 2
steps.why:
ADS 2, the filter envelope (attack, decay, sustain), flicks the resonant peak open on every note.
- ADS CONTROL 2.8 (+3.9 oct): well right of centre; how wide each squelch opens.
- ATTACK 1 (2 ms): immediate.
- DECAY 5.2 (77 ms): short, so it closes quickly. Longer turns the squelch into a slow wah.
- SUSTAIN 0: back to dark while held.
- Listen for: a wet “bwow” on every note.

steps.title: Turn the envelope upside down
steps.why:
The voltage processor adds and scales voltages, and its REV OUT puts the result out upside down. Fed with ADS 2, it gives a falling copy of the envelope for the scoop.
- Cable ADS 2 OUT → IN 2: the envelope into the voltage processor.
- IN 1 GAIN 0: removes the fixed +10 V that IN 1 carries when unpatched, so REV OUT carries only the envelope. Turned up, it would push every note flat.
- OUT GAIN 0.15: the depth of the scoop, kept small.
- Listen for: no change yet; REV OUT is not patched.

steps.title: Scoop the pitch
steps.why:
VCO MOD IN takes the LFO’s place on the pitch of both VCOs. Fed the upside-down envelope, it starts each note flat and lets it spring up to pitch. The Kobol has no glide, so this is how it slides.
- Cable REV OUT → VCO MOD IN: each note starts about three and a half semitones flat and rises as ADS 2 falls, in step with the squelch.
- Listen for: the bounce at the front of every note. Set OUT GAIN to 0 and the notes start dead on pitch; a longer ADS 2 DECAY turns the bounce into a slow slide.

steps.title: Tight, funky notes
steps.why:
ADS 1, the loudness envelope for the output VCA, keeps the funk tight.
- ATTACK 1 (2 ms): instant, so the scoop lands on the beat.
- DECAY 4.8 (55 ms), SUSTAIN 9: near-full level while held. DECAY is also the release: the length of each note’s tail once the key is up.
- Listen for: clean rests between notes, so the line stays in the pocket.

sounds.name: Dark Drifting Pad
sounds.ref: In the style of Brian Eno — "Zawinul/Lava" (Another Green World)
sounds.blurb: A slow, dark, slightly murky tone whose lower half keeps changing shape on its own.
sounds.how: VCO 1 is a soft triangle at the note played. VCO 2, an octave below, gets a very slow LFO patched into its WAVEFORM input, so over about ten seconds it turns from triangle to square and back. The filter is low with a little resonance, so the change is heard as a slow thickening and thinning rather than a sweep. Slow attacks and long releases let the notes blur into each other.

steps.title: A soft triangle on top
steps.why:
VCO 1, the voltage-controlled oscillator on top, is a soft, steady tone at the note played.
- VCO 1 WAVEFORM 1: near the triangle end, just into the ramp.
- VCO 1 VOLUME 7: its level through its own VCA (voltage-controlled amplifier).
- Listen for: a soft, round tone.

steps.title: VCO 2 an octave below
steps.why:
VCO 2 goes an octave below and a little brighter. This is the half that will change shape.
- VCO 2 FREQUENCY 4 (−12 st): an octave down.
- VCO 2 WAVEFORM 3.5: between ramp and sawtooth, the middle of its drift. Nearer 0 it spends more time soft; nearer 7 more time hollow.
- VCO 2 BEAT 0.5 (+5 cents): beats slightly against VCO 1.
- VCO 2 VOLUME 6: through its own VCA; the Kobol has no mixer.
- Listen for: a fuller tone with a slow beat.

steps.title: A very slow LFO on its shape
steps.why:
The LFO (low-frequency oscillator) is patched to VCO 2’s WAVEFORM input, so VCO 2 slowly turns from triangle towards square and back.
- Cable LFO OUT 2 → VCO 2 WAVEFORM: OUT 2 is the LFO at full level.
- LFO triangle, RATE 2.5 (0.10 Hz): about ten seconds per cycle.
- LFO VOLUME 0: this knob is the vibrato depth; at 0 nothing wobbles in pitch. LFO OUT 2 does not depend on it.
- Listen for: hold a note for twenty seconds and hear the lower half thicken and thin.

steps.title: A dark filter
steps.why:
The VCF (voltage-controlled filter) goes low with some resonance, and ADS 2, the filter envelope (attack, decay, sustain), opens it a little as each note swells in.
- VCF FREQ 4.6 (384 Hz), RESONANCE 3: dark and slightly murky, so VCO 2’s change is heard as thickening and thinning rather than a sweep.
- KEYB CTRL 0.8 (80 %): keyboard control; the cutoff mostly follows the notes.
- ADS CONTROL 1 (+1.4 oct): a small opening on each note.
- ADS 2 ATTACK 7.5, DECAY 9, SUSTAIN 6: a 550 ms rise and a 2.0 s fall. A slow rise, then an easy settle.
- Listen for: each note opening gently over half a second.

steps.title: Slow in, slow out
steps.why:
ADS 1, the loudness envelope, is slow in and slow out, so notes blur into each other.
- ATTACK 7.4 (510 ms): half a second of fade-in.
- DECAY 9.4 (2.8 s), SUSTAIN 9: near-full level while held. DECAY is also the release, so each note hangs on for nearly three seconds after you let go.
- Listen for: chords that fade under the next one, while the lower half keeps changing shape.

sounds.name: Steel Bender Swell
sounds.ref: In the style of Daniel Lanois — "Sioux Lookout" (Flesh and Machine)
sounds.blurb: A pedal-steel style swell: two voices fade in together, then the upper one bends up a whole tone while the lower one holds.
sounds.how: On a pedal steel a pedal raises one string while the others ring on. Here VCO 1 holds the note and VCO 2 sits a fifth above it. ADS 2, with a one-second attack, goes through the voltage processor into VCO 2 FREQ, so VCO 2 bends from the fifth up to the sixth as the note swells in. ADS 1’s slow attack stands in for the volume pedal, and a small, slow vibrato from the LFO is the steel bar moving on the strings.

steps.title: Two soft voices a fifth apart
steps.why:
Two VCOs (voltage-controlled oscillators) a fifth apart are the two strings: VCO 1 holds the note and VCO 2 will bend.
- WAVEFORM 2.5 on both: between triangle and ramp, round and singing.
- VCO 2 FREQUENCY 5.6 (+7 st): a fifth above VCO 1. Tune it by ear; each knob step is about an octave.
- VOLUME 7 and 5.5: each VCO has its own VCA (voltage-controlled amplifier) in place of a mixer.
- Listen for: an open, gentle fifth on every key.

steps.title: A warm filter
steps.why:
The VCF (voltage-controlled filter) sits in the middle, warm and following the keys. ADS 2 is kept off the filter, so it is free for the bend.
- VCF FREQ 5.6 (766 Hz), RESONANCE 2: warm, with a slight edge.
- KEYB CTRL 1 (100 %): keyboard control; the tone is even across the keys.
- ADS CONTROL 0 (off): no filter envelope.
- Listen for: a softer, warmer fifth.

steps.title: A slow envelope for the pedal
steps.why:
ADS 2 is an ADS (attack, decay, sustain) envelope. Here it is the pedal: a slow push down, then held.
- ATTACK 8.2 (1000 ms): rises over about a second. Lower makes the bend snap up at the start of the note.
- DECAY 9 (2.0 s): with SUSTAIN full it only acts on release, setting how slowly the pedal comes back up.
- SUSTAIN 10: holds at full, so the bend stays for as long as the key is down.
- Listen for: no change yet; ADS 2 is not patched anywhere.

steps.title: Bend VCO 2 with it
steps.why:
The voltage processor, a utility that adds and scales voltages, turns ADS 2 into a bend of the right size for VCO 2.
- ADS 2 OUT → IN 2, OUT → VCO 2 FREQ: two cables; the envelope goes through the voltage processor to VCO 2’s pitch only.
- IN 1 GAIN 0: removes the fixed +10 V that IN 1 carries when unpatched, which would put VCO 2 out of tune.
- OUT GAIN 0.083: makes the full envelope worth two semitones, a whole tone, from the fifth up to the sixth. 0.042 would be a semitone.
- Listen for: the upper voice rising while the lower one stays put.

steps.title: The volume pedal
steps.why:
ADS 1, the loudness envelope, stands in for the volume pedal: each note swells in with no pick and dies away slowly.
- ATTACK 7.8 (710 ms): a slow swell. Longer is slower.
- DECAY 9.4 (2.8 s), SUSTAIN 10: full level while held, then a long fade, as DECAY is also the release.
- Listen for: notes that fade in while the bend happens, like a pedal-steel player easing up the volume.

steps.title: Bar vibrato
steps.why:
The LFO (low-frequency oscillator) is wired to both VCOs’ pitch. A small, slow vibrato is the steel bar moving on the strings.
- LFO WAVEFORM triangle: a smooth waver.
- LFO RATE 6.2 (3.02 Hz): about three wavers a second.
- LFO VOLUME 0.7 (7 %): small. Above 1.5 it sounds seasick.
- Listen for: a slight waver on both voices while the bend holds.
